criterion_scores.reasoning: The guide is broadly coherent and gives actionable rules for voice, post architecture, CTAs, visual formats, and quality gates. However, I found consequential internal contradictions and suspect factual claims: the universal “physically being there” receipt floor conflicts with pre-event/upcoming-week formats (lines 45–46), the 4:5 screen-space math is likely wrong or at least unstated in its assumptions (lines 197–199), and carousel CTA guidance conflicts with the no-CTA post-event rule (lines 76 and 250).

Most required style-guide components are present at substantial depth: voice/tone, audience, architecture, data points, formatting, DMs, quality bar, positioning, and visual workflow. Provided deterministic checks report no missing .claude references. The main completeness gap is provenance: operationally important platform claims such as the LinkedIn character limit verification are not tied to a source or verification method, making them hard to audit or refresh.

Placement under .claude/references is appropriate for a reference document, and the file uses relative links to canonical internal docs/skills. The provided missing-reference and tombstone checks found no failures. I did not see project-skill naming, MCP-write, subagent fan-out, or command-skeleton convention issues because this is not a skill/command/hook. Minor uncertainty remains because no explicit reference-doc frontmatter convention was supplied.

The artifact mostly avoids tombstoned tools and keeps guidance tied to concrete production needs. However, it includes unsupported precise metrics and performance claims, especially the carousel engagement multiplier at lines 245–246 and the screen-space percentages at lines 197–199. Those are exactly the kind of fabricated specificity/orphan metric the rubric warns against if not sourced and scoped.

The document is legible and richly structured, but diagnostics are weakened by overconfident verification language without recorded evidence. Line 98 says the LinkedIn cap was “verified June 2026” without a source or method, while line 114 requires real verified resources for public claims. The internal contradictions around universal receipt floors and CTA rules are also not called out as exceptions, so failures would be confusing to downstream content generation.

defects.quote: ≥1 detail only possible from physically being there
defects.description: The rule is marked non-negotiable for every post, but the guide also covers Upcoming Week and Pre-Event posts where Alex has not physically been there yet. This creates an impossible universal requirement unless scoped to post-event or attended-event content.

The guide asserts a platform fact as verified but provides no source, method, or citation. Because the artifact itself treats verification/provenance as mandatory elsewhere, this is overconfident framing and triggers the confidence-honesty concern.
A key operational constraint is missing the provenance needed to refresh or audit it later. The document states it was verified but does not record where or how.

defects.quote: ~20% more vertical screen space than 1:1 and ~65% more than 16:9, which directly
defects.description: The aspect-ratio math is not supported as written. At equal width, 4:5 is 25% taller than 1:1 and much more than 65% taller than 16:9; if this is based on LinkedIn-specific feed rendering, the guide does not state the assumptions or source.

defects.quote: Carousels (uploaded as LinkedIn PDFs) get ~1.5-2x the engagement of single images
defects.description: This is a precise performance multiplier with no source, scope, or date. It risks fabricated specificity/orphan metric behavior in a style guide intended to govern production choices.

defects.quote: "Follow for more" or a specific question that drives comments.
defects.description: This carousel-final-slide CTA guidance is not reconciled with the post-event recap rule at line 76: “No CTA. Pure documentarian.” If a post-event recap uses a carousel, the guide gives conflicting instructions.
